toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The evidence points to one chance QC outlier on Analyzer B, not a faulty analyzer or bad reagent lot. The repeat of the same vial passed. Level 1 and Level 3 were normal. Sodium and chloride were normal. There were no other QC rule violations in a month. Level 2 averages did not move after the lot change. Patient results re-run on Analyzer A agreed within 0.02 mmol/L on average. QC ran on schedule (182 of 182), so skipped QC from short staffing is not supported. A short sample or bubble can't be excluded, so I would not record it as the confirmed cause.

Ward 6's high potassiums split 7 on Analyzer A and 7 on Analyzer B. They coincide with the tube outage (long transit times) and with four renal overflow patients. Delayed transport is a plausible explanation, but it is only an association so far.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B potassium to service and add an extra Level 2 QC at the start of each shift for a week. Do not recall about 2,900 results, quarantine the lot, or widen the limits to ±4 SD. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples on current high results and get the tube fixed. Tell Dr Larkby the analyzers are not giving false highs.
